title: One-Sitting Idle: incremental games designed to end in 30–60 minutes, with a story and no ads
user: Incremental/idle fans on HN who like the genre's mechanics but hate endless grinds, dark-pattern monetisation and games that never conclude.

evidence.quote_or_summary: A Dark Room has storytelling and an ending, which is uncommon in incremental games.
Players want clear, fair progression to an endpoint rather than learning-by-dying mechanics.
Positive reception of a roughly 30-minute incremental game with defined levels.
Community backlash against ads and micro-donations in an A-Dark-Room-like game.

smallest_useful_product: One 45-minute lighthouse episode: light to shipping to town to storm finale, with three acts, mechanical twists, a real ending, completion time, and portable local saves.
success_measure: At least 40% of starters reach the ending; median completion time 35–60 minutes; at least 25% of finishers play a second episode when released.
monetization: The launch episode is free. A one-time paid season may be offered only when later episodes exist; never ads or micro-donations.
constraints: Original theme, art and text; telemetry-free playtesting; pure-keyboard play; no prestige loops, daily rewards, ads, IAP, or offline-earnings dark patterns.
